translations.translatedText: # Monday 26.8.2019 (radio)
The Porvoo police shooters were caught after a wild car chase. Groundwater is low. Young girls in particular move too little. Time magazine says that Oodi is the library of the future.
## Porvoo shooting case

![Police on the E12 road between Hämeenkyrö and Ikaalinen on 25 August. The police caught two people at the end of a car chase in the Tampere area.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10938999)
Open image viewer
The police caught two men after a car chase in Ikaalinen. Photo: Mika Kanerva / Lehtikuva
The police have arrested 2 men who are suspected of shooting at police officers in Porvoo.
The men are Swedish citizens. One of the men is also a Finnish dual citizen. According to Yle's information, both men speak Finnish and Swedish.

The men were caught on Sunday evening in Ikaalinen, near Tampere. They were caught after a wild car chase. During the chase the men fired about 10 shots at the police. In addition, 3 police cars were damaged. However, nobody was injured in the chase.

The men are suspected of shooting at 2 police officers in Porvoo during the night between Saturday and Sunday. One police officer was seriously injured, but is not in danger of his life. The other police officer has already been discharged from hospital.
The shooters are suspected of 2 attempted murders.
## Low groundwater
![Maintenance man repairing a dried-up ring well in Hollola.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10935313)
Open image viewer
A maintenance man repairs a dried-up well in Hollola. Photo: Petri Niemi / Yle
Groundwater is now very low in many places. It is so low that many wells are in danger of running out of water.

Groundwater is low, for example, in Southern, Western and Central Finland and in North Savo. The Finnish Environment Institute says that groundwater levels are up to 50 centimetres lower than usual at this time of year.
Hydrogeologist Petri Siiro says that small showers are not enough to raise the groundwater. Now heavy rain that lasts a long time is needed.
## How Finns move
![Terrain walks are best suited for Nordic walking.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9751683)
Open image viewer
More than half of adults move at least 3 hours a week. Photo: Markku Lähdetluoma / Yle
Finns exercise more than before. Even so, many move less than is recommended.
A study by the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare says that over 50 per cent of adults move enough, that is, at least 3 hours a week.
Comprehensive school pupils, upper secondary school pupils and vocational school students move less than recommended, that is, under 7 hours a week. Boys exercise more than girls.
## Oodi gets praise

![A view over the third floor of the Oodi central library. A woman sits on a sofa working on her computer.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_6756,h_3800,x_0,y_306/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-5337655c2607f75a5b2/1545996415)
Open image viewer
Oodi's book sky. Photo: Yle / Lukas Rusk
The American magazine Time praises Helsinki's central library Oodi.
Time has listed the 100 most interesting places in the world. One of them is Oodi.
Time says that Oodi is the library of the future. The magazine tells, for example, that Oodi has robots, game rooms and recording studios.
In addition to Oodi, Time's list includes, for example, parks, restaurants and cultural sites.
